index_only.includes: BoundStudent.decide_index_one(situation (S,)) -> candidate index: input checks and the out_of_range policy -> encode_one -> SpikingNetwork.decide_one (numpy); the candidate lookup and the bounds check are not included

latency.label: wall-clock latency of the deployed numpy decision path on this machine (a measurement)
latency.protocol: learned_judgment.eval.harness.measure_latency, once for full_path and then once for index_only over the same situations: call i decides situation i mod n; each call is timed alone with time.perf_counter_ns; no warm-up calls; median and p95 (numpy 'linear' quantile) over all calls

caveats: Energy figures are analytical estimates from operation counts and published 45 nm CMOS per-operation energies. They are not measurements. The networks ran on a CPU laptop with dense matrix arithmetic, where a spiking network does not save energy.

The estimate counts arithmetic only. Memory accesses for weights and membrane state, data movement, addressing, static power and spike communication are excluded, although published analyses find that memory accesses dominate.

The result depends on conventions: arithmetic precision, whether the real-valued first layer is counted once or at every time step, and whether neuron leak, bias and reset updates are counted. The variant including neuron updates is reported next to the main estimate.

The dense reference is a non-spiking network with the same layer sizes whose operation count follows from its architecture. No such network was trained, so the comparison says nothing about whether it would reach the same decision quality.
Teacher (TabPFN) inference energy is not included. The comparison is per student decision.

dense_reference_estimate.definition: e_mac x sum over layers of fan_in x fan_out: one pass through a non-spiking dense network with the same layer sizes (no such network was trained)

h4_energy_criterion.rule: PREREGISTRATION.md, amendment 2026-11-21 "how H4's energy criterion is judged": two estimates are reported for the SNN, each with an interval: the convention common in the SNN literature (real-valued first layer plus one accumulate per synaptic event), and the same plus every neuron's leak, input and reset update. The reference is the non-spiking dense network of the same layer sizes. H4's energy criterion is supported only if both estimates are below the reference, not supported if both are above it, and inconclusive if they disagree. Applied here to each estimate's mean per decision over the measured situations; a mean equal to the reference is neither below nor above it, which makes the verdict inconclusive.
h4_energy_criterion.scope: H4's energy criterion only, for this network on these situations. H4's error criterion (within 25% of the teacher's error) is judged separately on simulator episodes. Every energy figure is an estimate from operation counts and cited per-operation energies, not a measurement.

energy_estimate.label: estimate, 45 nm CMOS, arithmetic only; not a measurement

break_even.definition: under the main estimate hidden layer l's spikes cost e_ac per synapse per spike and its dense synapses cost e_mac once per decision, so connection l costs less than its dense counterpart when its firing rate per step is below e_mac / (e_ac T); the estimate is below the dense reference exactly when the H_l x fo_l weighted rate is
break_even.weights_definition: H_l x fo_l (synapses from hidden layer l to the layer it feeds)

main_estimate.definition: e_mac x first-layer MACs (D x H_1, once per decision) + e_ac x synaptic operations (spikes x fan-out)

estimate_pj_interval.resampled_unit: distinct situation (sha256 of its values) with all of its rows; the statistic of a resample is the mean over the rows it contains (sum over the drawn situations / their row count), so the estimate is the row mean
estimate_pj_interval.statistic: mean main energy estimate per decision (pJ)

main_estimate.interval_vs_dense_reference_estimate: entirely below the dense reference estimate

ratio_interval.definition: estimate_pj_interval divided by the dense reference estimate (a constant per decision)

break_even.definition: the estimate including neuron updates is below the dense reference exactly when the H_l x (fo_l + 1) weighted firing rate per step is below this rate; when the rate is <= 0 the neuron updates alone cost at least as much as the dense reference's synapses after the first layer, so no firing rate reaches it
break_even.formula: (e_mac * sum_l H_l fo_l - (e_mac + e_ac) * (sum_l H_l + C) * T) / (e_ac * T * sum_l H_l (fo_l + 1))
break_even.weights_definition: H_l x (fo_l + 1) (synapses from hidden layer l plus one reset subtraction per spike)

with_neuron_updates_estimate.definition: main estimate + (e_mac + e_ac) x neuron updates ((sum_l H_l + C) x T) + e_ac x spikes (one reset subtraction each)

estimate_pj_interval.resampled_unit: distinct situation (sha256 of its values) with all of its rows; the statistic of a resample is the mean over the rows it contains (sum over the drawn situations / their row count), so the estimate is the row mean
estimate_pj_interval.statistic: mean energy estimate with neuron updates per decision (pJ)

with_neuron_updates_estimate.interval_vs_dense_reference_estimate: entirely below the dense reference estimate

ratio_interval.definition: estimate_pj_interval divided by the dense reference estimate (a constant per decision)

firing.neuron_definitions: never fire: no spike at any step on any of these situations; fire every step: a spike at every step on every one of these situations
firing.rate_definition: mean fraction of a hidden layer's neurons firing per time step, over the situations
firing.source: per-neuron spike trains of SpikingNetwork.forward_with_spike_trains on the counted inputs

operations.label: operation counts measured by running the deployed numpy network on the given situations; every energy figure is an estimate from those counts, not a measurement

spike_train_check.source: SpikingNetwork.forward_with_spike_trains against snn_core.count_operations on the same inputs

interval_total.resampled_unit: distinct situation (sha256 of its values) with all of its rows; the statistic of a resample is the mean over the rows it contains (sum over the drawn situations / their row count), so the estimate is the row mean
interval_total.statistic: mean spikes per decision (all hidden layers)

synaptic_ops_per_decision.definition: sum over hidden layers of spikes emitted x fan-out (the width of the layer they feed)

interval.resampled_unit: distinct situation (sha256 of its values) with all of its rows; the statistic of a resample is the mean over the rows it contains (sum over the drawn situations / their row count), so the estimate is the row mean

out_of_scope: decision quality on actual Go2 episodes is measured by learned_judgment.eval.harness on the simulator, not in this record

student.n_inputs_note: the network's input width D; larger than the situation encoding's width when the network is one skill's view of a shared network (padding and skill-slot inputs)

student_meta.decision_runtime: numpy (learned_judgment.students.snn_core); torch was used for training only

dream.score_spread_rows: training rows (null under target_spread 'per_row': each row uses its own)
dream.split: by distinct situation (learned_judgment.students.snn.split_rows_by_situation): rows with identical situations are all training rows or all early-stopping rows

early_stopping_rows_in_dream.spread_definition: median population std of the training rows' scores (dream.training_row_spread)

student_meta.label: dream-trained spiking student: trained to choose the candidate the dream scores best; every number here is measured inside the dream, not in the simulator; the numbers under 'early_stopping_rows_in_dream' come from the rows that chose the restored weights, so they are not held-out numbers

parity.rows: every training and early-stopping row of the dream

candidate_grid.definition: sha256 over b'learned-judgment/candidate-grid/v1', points_per_dim, and for each probe situation the shape and float64 bytes of spec.candidate_actions(situation, points_per_dim) (-0.0 written as 0.0)

situation_variables.description: fixture: lateral offset of the approaching object
situation_variables.name: fx_offset

situations_seen.definition: sha256 over b'learned-judgment/situation/v1', b'float64:<S>' and the S float64 values of the situation (-0.0 written as 0.0); identical situations have identical digests

training.acceptance: the restored weights must have a total validation KL below initialisation, a validation KL per head below that of the head's mean training target (the best constant prediction), and spikes in every hidden layer on the validation rows; otherwise fit raises TrainingError
training.loss: per head KL(target || softmax(logits)) averaged over that head's rows, weighted by the head's share of the batch, plus spike_rate_penalty x mean hidden firing rate; early stopping on the sampling-weighted validation KL
